title: Anaxia, the BLLM engine (eBLLM 2.1): verifier-gated conjecture closure, the BLLM crossing network and the BLLM paper

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India; Formerly, University of Calcutta, Senate House, 87/1 College Street, Kolkata 700073, West Bengal, India

description:
Anaxia is the BLLM engine, published as the Python package eBLLM, a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine. Version 1 implemented the verifier-gated VSI circuit: a conjecture becomes a typed package, an attempt becomes an obligation graph, and a result is released only when every verifier factor is 1. Version 2 adds the BLLM system of D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya, BLLM: The Entropy Cost of Sound Self-Improvement and a Typed Crossing Network Tested on Five Open Problems (2026): entropy-law check schedules; a typed crossing network of known constructions, in which a candidate fills an input of one construction with the output of another and every closed candidate is checked by a program and attacked by a refuter; booster weights; a shared SQLite memory with retrieval; target points; an attack channel; five target agents and a continuous loop; language-model, local-model and non-model proposers; and the benchmark on the lattice mass gap of Yang–Mills theory, the Hodge conjecture, Grothendieck's standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdős problem 1183. None of the five problems is solved, and no pass line is crossed; the logs of every run are included.

The experiments folder holds the exact and weighted-poset searches for Erdős problem 1183 (exact values of f(n) for n up to 20, where the lower bound at n = 20 is the twenty-level window of the fifth version of Bhattacharjee, Mandal and Bhattacharya, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23374973; the analysis of m-sequence colourings; the grid-colouring searches at n = 20), the forest gauge fixing for SU(2) lattice Yang–Mills with its Lean statements, a Monte Carlo scout of the Dobrushin–Shlosman condition on boxes (estimates, not proofs), a LoRA fine-tuning script for the local proposer, and a hardware check. The Lean library has 30 theorems, each depending only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; 65 unit tests and C, C++ and Julia checks run in CI.

Version 2.1 names the engine Anaxia (command anaxia; ebllm remains), rebuilds and publishes the container image on every merge to main and every release after the version, the command line and the Lean axiom audit pass inside it, lets a running image tell whether a newer one is published (anaxia update), and makes this repository the home of the BLLM paper: its source, its Lean development of 59 theorems with Mathlib and its checks are in paper/bllm, with their history from creelie/D7.
